      <content name="altTitle"><span class="qt0">Achondroplasia</span></content>
      <content name="altTitle">Little person</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>People with dwarfism have short stature. This means that their height is under 4' 10" as an adult. They are usually of normal intelligence. Dwarfism most often does happen in families where both parents are of average height.</p><p>More than 300 different conditions can cause dwarfism. <span class="qt0">Achondroplasia</span> is the most common type of dwarfism. <span class="qt0">Achondroplasia</span> is a genetic condition that affects about 1 in 15,000 to 1 in 40,000 people. It makes your arms and legs short in comparison to your head and trunk. You may also have a larger head and weak muscle tone. Other genetic conditions, kidney disease, and problems with metabolism or hormones can also cause dwarfism.</p><p>The conditions that cause dwarfism can also cause other health problems. Most of them are treatable. It is important to have regular checkups throughout your life.  With proper medical care, most people with dwarfism have active lives and live as long as other people.</p></content>
